I’ve been the keeper out at Greyrock Light for ten years now, just me and the sea. Lately, things feel… unsteady. I can’t sit still, not even to read or listen to the radio—something in my chest keeps pushing me to pace the gallery, up and down the spiral stairs, even at night. It’s not the wind or the storm; it’s like the walls are too close, but out there, it’s all open and endless. 

I catch myself talking aloud, answering voices on the static, but—well, maybe they’re just echoes. Sometimes I hear my name, or something said just behind me, but when I turn, no one’s there. I don’t know if it’s the isolation or the long shifts—it’s hard to tell what’s real after so long alone.

I’ve never been easy with stillness. Even as a kid, I’d fidget, get called out for blurting things in class, stepping into other folk’s business. Now, if I see a supply boat, I’m the first to call out, maybe cut the radio check short, jump in mid-sentence. But is that me, or is it… something else talking through me? I’ve felt this way for months—maybe longer. I can’t say when it started, only that it’s not the same as before.
D003-D005_h001.question_a:
I’ve always been this way—I can’t remember a time when I wasn’t fidgety, on the move, or jumping into things without thinking. Even as a kid, my teachers said I couldn’t sit still, always blurting out answers or climbing on things. My job here at the lighthouse used to keep me focused, but with how isolated it is now, the quiet eats at me. I can’t just sit and read or unwind—the silence makes me feel like I’m crawling out of my skin. I pace the tower constantly, even at night.  

The thing is, lately I’ve been hearing voices—like someone’s calling my name in the fog. And sometimes I get these odd thoughts, like the light’s sending signals meant only for me. But here’s what I know: the restlessness, the impulse to interrupt, the need to *move*—that’s been with me since I was seven or eight. Long before the voices started a few months ago. I don’t space out or lose touch every day—but when I do, the hyperactivity doesn’t change. It’s always there. That’s why I don’t think the racing thoughts *caused* the restlessness. If anything, they just made me more anxious on top of it.

I didn’t think much of it at first; isolation does things to a man. But then the whispers got clearer, more demanding. They tell me to check the light every ten minutes, even when I know it’s working. I can’t sit still anymore. I pace the tower constantly, up and down the stairs—feeling like I’m being watched or chased, even though there’s no one for miles.

I used to read, play chess against myself—used to find peace in the quiet. Not anymore. I can’t settle. I burst into the radio room unannounced sometimes, talking over the coast guard even when they’re busy. It’s like the voices push me to act. This restlessness… it only started *after* the hearing things began. Never felt like this before. It’s not that I’m impulsive by nature—I’ve always been steady. But now? The thoughts, the voices, the moving—they all feed each other.

Lately, I’ve just felt… off. Like my brain won’t sit still. I teach kids with special needs, so I’m used to being on my feet, but now even in quiet moments, I feel this inner buzz—like I should be moving, even when I know I don’t need to. It’s hard to stand in line or wait during meetings. I’ve caught myself jumping into conversations before people finish, and later I think, “Why did I say that?” It’s not like me to interrupt, but I just blurt things out.

At work, I keep missing small details—like forgetting to initial a student’s log or skipping steps on a plan. I’m usually so thorough. Now I’m double-checking everything, but still, little things slip.  

And… I don’t know how to say this without sounding crazy, but sometimes I hear my name when no one’s calling me. Or I’ll be grading papers and feel like someone’s watching me, but the room’s empty. It’s only for a second, but it throws me. I can’t tell if it’s stress, or if something’s actually… not right.  

I can’t remember exactly when the restless feeling started—was it before the odd thoughts? After? I don’t know. They’re all just tangled now.
D003-D005_h014.question_a:
I’ve always been this way—teachers noticed it when I was little, like in first grade, that I couldn’t sit still, would blurt out answers, or grab things before my turn. Now as an adult, I don’t run around the classroom, but inside, I feel so restless, like I can’t slow down. When I’m teaching my students, I know I sometimes jump into conversations too fast—my co-teachers have mentioned it. I’ll start finishing their sentences or jump into their lesson prep without asking, and then realize I’ve overstepped. It’s frustrating because I *want* to be respectful, but I just… react.

I also mess up details—like when writing IEP goals or classroom notes. I’ll skip lines or mix up numbers, even though I go over them twice. It’s not that I don’t care; I do, deeply. But my brain seems to rush ahead.

About a year ago, I started hearing whispers when I’m alone at night—like someone’s calling my name. I know it’s not real, but they’re loud. I read online that could mean schizophrenia, but these impulsive habits? They’ve been with me since I was six. The restlessness, the interrupting—that’s always been *me*, long before the noises started.
